newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikko says fire could cost Toyota over 40 bln yen.
newsitem.headline: Nikko says fire could cost Toyota over 40 bln yen.

text.p: Lost production after a fire last weekend at a key parts supplier could cost Toyota Motor Corp more than 40 billion yen on an operating profit basis, Nikko Research Center said on Thursday.
The private research body said in a report that Toyota's production was likely to recover to an average of only 15 percent of capacity this week and to an average of 60 percent next week.
Even if output could be raised to full capacity next week as Toyota hopes, the fire would still cost the company about 18.5 billion yen, the research body said.

The fire on Saturday at Aisin Seiki Co Ltd's Kariya plant prevented output of brake parts supplied to Toyota, forcing the idling of all the car makers' domestic plants on Tuesday, except for those of Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd, and halting 22 out of a total of 30 production lines on Monday.
Toyota said on Tuesday that its production would return to near-normal levels on Friday and, with overtime work, to normal levels from the beginning of next week.
Nikko said the costs of lost production could be absorbed by income from the weaker yen against the dollar.
Industry analysts say a decline of one yen against the dollar translates into 16 billion yen for Toyota.
In November Toyota assumed an average yen/dollar rate of 107 for 1996/97 when forecasting a parent operating profit of 450 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1997.
The yen was trading at around 123 to the dollar on Thursday.
